intro: To say that a car belongs to Paul, English says “Paul's car”: first the owner, then 's, then the thing. You need this structure to talk about your family, your friends and the things that belong to them.
objectifs: Build the possessive: owner + 's + thing, in the right order.
Put the apostrophe in the right place in the singular, in plurals with -s (my parents') and in irregular plurals (children's).
Use the possessive with no noun after it (at Marie's, at the doctor's).

texte: In English, the owner comes first: owner + 's + thing → Paul's car. There is no article before the thing: don't say “the Paul's car”.
The owner can be a first name, a family name, or a noun with its determiner: my sister's room, the teacher's desk, our neighbour's dog.

lignes: the car that belongs to Paul

texte: Singular: add 's → the boy's bag (one boy).
Regular plural with -s: add only the apostrophe after the s → the boys' bags (several boys), my parents' house. When you speak, boy's, boys and boys' sound the same: the situation helps.
Irregular plural with no -s (children, men, women, people): add 's → the children's room, women's rights, people's opinions.
Names ending in s: both forms exist: James's car or James' car. “James's” is more common in modern British English.

lignes: my brothers' flat (two or more brothers)
the men's team, the children's toys

sections.titre: Two owners, and no noun after 's
texte: When two people own one thing together, put 's only after the second name: Paul and Marie's flat (they share it). If each person has their own, put 's after both: Paul's and Marie's cars.

You can leave out the noun after 's when it is clear: Whose bag is this? — It's Ana's. This is very common with places: at my aunt's (= at my aunt's house), at the doctor's, at the hairdresser's, the baker's (the bakery).
exemples: We're having dinner at Julie's tonight.
I've got an appointment at the dentist's.
at the dentist's = at the dentist's surgery.
Whose keys are these? — They're Omar's.
Tom and Lisa's wedding is in June.
sections.note: “Whose?” is the question for possession: Whose phone is this? Don't confuse it with “Who's” (= who is): they sound the same.

texte: Use 's mainly with people, animals, countries, organisations and time expressions: my friend's car, the cat's food, Canada's capital, the company's results, today's newspaper, a week's holiday.
With things, use “the … of …”: the end of the film, the name of the street, the door of the car. For some common pairs, you can also put a noun before a noun: the car door, the street name.
With a long owner (several words), “of” is also more natural: the house of the family next door (not “the family next door's house”).

lignes: my aunt's garden, the dog's bed
the top of the page, the kitchen window
the name of the woman in the red dress

sections.titre: The 's trap: is, has or possessive?
texte: The letters 's can mean three things: “is” (She's French), “has” (She's got a car) or possession (Sophie's car). To know which, look at the next word: a noun → possession; an adjective, a noun with an article or an -ing verb → is; got → has.
Don't confuse possession with the plural: “my friends” (more than one friend, no apostrophe), “my friend's car” (the car of my friend).
exemples: Marc's got a new car. → Marc has got a new car.

formule: owner + 's + noun (Paul's car) · plural with -s + ' (my parents' house) · irregular plural + 's (children's toys)
prononciation: 's sounds like the plural -s: /s/ after p, t, k, f (Pat's /pæts/), /z/ after a vowel or voiced sound (Paul's /pɔːlz/), /ɪz/ after s, z, sh, ch, j sounds (Alice's /ˈælɪsɪz/, George's /ˈdʒɔːdʒɪz/).
“parents'” sounds exactly like “parents”: /ˈpeərənts/. You can't hear the apostrophe.
“James's” is /ˈdʒeɪmzɪz/, with an extra syllable; “James'” is usually /dʒeɪmz/.
In “at the doctor's”, stress DOC-: /ət ðə ˈdɒktəz/.
erreurs: Plural with -s: apostrophe after the s.
Paul's and Marie's flat (they share it)
One thing, two owners: 's only after the second name.
The question for possession is whose.
A simple plural has no apostrophe.

dialogue.contexte: After a party in a flat in Brussels, two friends tidy up and find things people forgot.
lignes: Whose jacket is this? It's on the sofa.
Whose? = who does it belong to?
I think it's Yannick's. He's always got a black jacket.
And these keys? Are they your brother's?
No, they're my parents'. They're for their car. My mum's going to call me, I'm sure!
parents': plural owner; mum's = mum is.
Ha ha. And look, the children's drawings are on the table.
Those are my sister's kids. They're at my aunt's tonight.
at my aunt's = at my aunt's house.
OK. Is the last piece of cake for anyone?
the last piece of cake: of with things.
Yes! It's for Mariam and Léo's little girl. It's her favourite.
Two parents, one girl: 's after the second name.

mots: used to ask who something belongs to
My neighbour's dog is very noisy.
a person who lives near you (US: neighbor)
the sister of your mother or father
My uncle's farm is in Bafang.
the brother of your mother or father
My cousin's wedding is on Saturday.
the child of your aunt or uncle
My grandmother's cooking is the best.
the mother of your mother or father
the person who manages you at work
Tom and Lisa's wedding is in June.
the ceremony when two people get married
I've got an appointment at the dentist's.

exercices.consigne: Add the apostrophe in the right place.

items: (the end of the story / the story's end)
(the phone of my brother / my brother's phone)
(the top of the page / the page's top)

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.
items: The Marie's flat is very nice.
My parent's car is red. (both parents)
The mens room is on the left.
The men's room is on the left.
This is the computer of Anna.

exercices.consigne: Use the words to write a sentence with 's or '.
items: she / be / the wife of my brother
I / sleep / at the home of my cousin / tonight
I'm sleeping at my cousin's tonight.
the toys of the children / be / in the garden
The children's toys are in the garden.
whose bag / this? — it / belong to / Fatou
Whose bag is this? — It's Fatou's.

exercices.consigne: Write four sentences about your family or friends with 's: someone's job or name, a thing that belongs to someone, a place (at my…'s), and a sentence with a plural (my parents').
items: My sister's name is Inès. My best friend's car is a small red Fiat. On Sundays we have lunch at my grandmother's. My parents' house is near the river.

a_retenir: Owner + 's + thing, no article: Paul's car, my sister's room.
Plural with -s → ' (my parents' house); irregular plural → 's (children's, women's).
No noun after: It's Ana's; at my aunt's, at the doctor's.
's for people, animals, time; of for things (the end of the film).
Whose? = who does it belong to? ≠ who's (= who is).
